The rules for determining customs value are based on the general principles and rules set forth in Article Seven of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and in the Agreement on the Application of Article Seven of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.

The customs value of imported goods is determined by applying the following six methods: the transaction value of the imported goods, the transaction value of identical goods, the transaction value of similar goods, the deductive value method, the computed value method, and the fallback method.

The transaction value method for imported goods provides for the determination of the customs value of the goods based on the transaction value, that is, the price actually paid or payable for the goods at the time of crossing the customs border, adjusted taking into account the relevant rules.

When determining the customs value of imported goods, if these costs are not included in the transaction price, the costs incurred until the goods are delivered to the place of entry into the customs territory, and the costs incurred by the buyer, are added to the transaction price.

When determining the customs value of imported goods, the costs of installation, assembly, adjustment of equipment, transport costs after the goods have been brought into the customs territory, as well as customs duties and other payments payable in the Republic of Uzbekistan, must be excluded from the transaction price, if they are paid by the seller.

The transaction value method for imported goods cannot be used if there are restrictions on the buyer's rights to use the goods, if the goods were imported under a transaction without a value basis, if the terms of sale are dependent on conditions that cannot be taken into account, if a part of the proceeds from the subsequent resale of the goods goes to the seller and adjustments cannot be made, as well as.

The identical goods transaction value method provides for the acceptance of the transaction value of identical goods as the basis for determining the customs value of goods being imported into the customs territory.

An identical good means a good that is identical to the appraised good in terms of physical characteristics, quality, and market value, produced in the same country as the appraised good, sold for import into the Republic of Uzbekistan, and produced by the exact same person who produced the appraised good.
If several transactions for identical goods are identified, the transaction for identical goods with the lowest price shall be used to determine the customs value of the appraised good.

The transactional value method for similar goods provides that the value of a transaction for similar goods shall be taken as the basis for determining the customs value of the good being imported into the customs territory.

A similar good means a good that, although not identical in all respects to the appraised good, possesses similar characteristics and is similar in composition, allowing it to perform the same functions and be commercially interchangeable with it.

The deductive value method provides that the price per unit of the appraised, identical, or similar good, sold in large quantities in an unchanged condition in the customs territory within ninety calendar days prior to the import of the appraised good into the customs territory, shall be taken as the basis for determining the customs value of the appraised good.

The computed value method provides that the price calculated by adding the value of materials, manufacturing and processing costs, the amount of general expenses and profit obtained by the exporter, and other expenses, shall be taken as the basis for determining the customs value of the appraised good.

The fallback method, if the customs value of the good cannot be determined by other methods, provides that the customs value of the appraised good shall be determined by applying with some flexibility the requirements of the customs valuation methods regarding the application of time limits, and the determination of the country of origin, identity, or similarity of the goods.

To determine the customs value of a good using the fallback method, the selling price of a similar good produced in the Republic of Uzbekistan, a system that provides for taking the higher of two alternative values, the price of the good in the domestic market of the exporting country, production costs, and the price of the good delivered from the exporting country to third countries, shall be taken as the basis.

An event consisting of obtaining information through direct communication with a person who possesses information significant for solving the tasks of operational-investigative activities is called an inquiry.

According to the Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan "On Operational-Investigative Activities," the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the State Security Service, the State Security Service of the President, the military intelligence of the Ministry of Defense, the State Customs Committee, the Department for Combating Economic Crimes under the General Prosecutor's Office, and the Bureau of Compulsory Enforcement are the bodies that carry out operational-investigative activities.

An event aimed at obtaining information about individuals and legal entities, facts, and circumstances by studying documents, materials, databases, and sending questionnaires is called information gathering.

Eavesdropping on conversations conducted via telephones and other telecommunication devices, obtaining information transmitted through them, monitoring postal, courier, and telegraphic messages, as well as obtaining information about connections between subscribers or subscriber devices, is carried out on the basis of a court decision.

An event consisting of obtaining material objects for future comparative examination for the purpose of solving the tasks of operational-investigative activities is called collecting samples for comparative examination.

The main tasks of operational-investigative activities are to ensure the protection of human rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests, the property of legal and physical persons, the security of the individual, society, and the state, to collect information about persons, events, and actions that threaten the security of the individual, society, and the state, as well as to prevent, detect, suppress, and expose crimes.

An event consisting of purchasing goods or services for a fee from legal or physical persons that are significant for solving the tasks of operational-investigative activities is called a test purchase.

The main principles of operational-search activity are the principles of legality and conspiracy, the principle of the priority of human rights, freedoms, and legitimate interests, as well as the principle of combining overt and covert methods.

An activity consisting of concluding a fictitious transaction is called a controlled acquisition. This activity involves acquiring goods, currency valuables, substances, and other items without the intention of consuming or selling them, in order to identify and document a violation of the law.
An activity conducted with the involvement of specialists for the purpose of solving the tasks of operational-search activity is called the examination of items and documents.

An activity consisting of covertly observing and recording the actions of individuals, events, and processes for the purpose of obtaining information relevant to solving the tasks of operational-search activity is called operational surveillance.
An activity consisting of identifying or determining the identity of a person being checked or sought based on their distinctive features is called establishing the identity of a person.

An activity consisting of inspecting and studying residences and other places, buildings, structures, land plots, computers, communication devices, and vehicles for the purpose of identifying individuals, facts, and circumstances relevant to solving the tasks of operational-search activity is called the inspection of residences and other places, buildings, structures, land plots.
An activity consisting of covertly selecting and studying postal, courier, and telegraphic correspondence is called the control of postal, courier, and telegraphic correspondence.

An activity consisting of covertly listening to, intercepting, and recording conversations conducted using special technical means is called listening to conversations conducted via telephones and other telecommunication devices, and obtaining information transmitted through them.

An activity consisting of covertly obtaining information about the date, time, and duration of connections between subscribers or subscriber devices, and other data, is called obtaining information about connections between subscribers or subscriber devices.

An activity consisting of introducing an employee of the operational-search body or a person assisting on a confidential basis into a criminal-criminogenic environment or an object of operational significance is called operational introduction.

An activity consisting of covertly monitoring the movement of goods, currency valuables, substances, and other items whose free sale is prohibited or whose circulation is restricted is called a controlled delivery.
An activity consisting of covertly utilizing the capabilities of a person introduced into a criminal-criminogenic environment or an object of operational significance is called a disguised operation.
This activity, carried out with the aim of exposing and identifying individuals who have committed or are preparing to commit an unlawful act, is called an operational experiment.
